original_question: What are the best possible lower and upper bounds for the i-th adjacency eigenvalue of an n-vertex graph?
target_in_paper: Section 19.1, Problem 11 (Hong): the general problem stated immediately after the discussion of Powers’s Problem 10, asking for the sharp lower and upper bounds for the i-th eigenvalue of graphs with n vertices.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation. It correctly asks for best possible lower and upper bounds, for the i-th adjacency eigenvalue, over graphs with n vertices. That matches the scope of Hong’s general problem in Section 19.1 rather than the narrower preceding Problem 10, which only concerns upper bounds for the cases i = 3, 4.
missing_details: The paper’s ambient graph class is: simple, undirected, unweighted graphs.
The eigenvalues are those of the adjacency matrix A(G), not of the Laplacian or signless Laplacian.
The phrase “i-th eigenvalue” should be made stand-alone by specifying the ordering λ1(G) ≥ λ2(G) ≥ ··· ≥ λn(G), so this means the i-th largest adjacency eigenvalue.
The quantifier over i is implicit in the draft; to be fully stand-alone, state that 1 ≤ i ≤ n.
The problem is over all graphs of order n; there is no connectedness assumption in Problem 11.
No extra restrictions such as degree conditions, regularity, homogeneity, polynomial degree, ambient field changes, or nilpotency assumptions are part of this problem.
refined_question: For a simple, undirected, unweighted graph G on n vertices, let A(G) be its adjacency matrix and let λ1(G) ≥ λ2(G) ≥ ··· ≥ λn(G) be the eigenvalues of A(G). For each index i with 1 ≤ i ≤ n, determine the sharp universal lower bound and the sharp universal upper bound for λi(G) over all such n-vertex graphs.
justification: The draft clearly targets Hong’s general extremal-eigenvalue question, not Powers’s narrower one. In the introduction, the paper fixes the setting to simple, undirected, unweighted graphs, defines the adjacency matrix A(G), and orders its eigenvalues as λ1(G) ≥ ··· ≥ λn(G) (Introduction, p. 33). Then, in Section 19.1, after discussing Powers’s upper-bound question for i = 3, 4 and explicitly saying it is worth considering “the general question posed by Hong,” the paper states Problem 11: “Find the best possible lower and upper bounds for the i-th eigenvalue of graphs with n vertices” (Section 19.1, Problem 11, pp. 51-52). Your draft is therefore already paper-faithful in substance, but it leaves implicit the graph class, the adjacency-matrix operator, the eigenvalue ordering, and the quantifier 1 ≤ i ≤ n. Making those conventions explicit yields a mathematically complete stand-alone version without broadening the problem.
